sanskrit: anaḍvān dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyām utāmūm anaḍvān dādhārorv antarikṣam | anaḍvān dādhāra pradiśaḥ ṣaḍ urvīr anaḍvān idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam ā viveśa ||
english: The bull (anaḍvān) upholds the earth and yonder sky; the bull upholds the wide midspace. The bull upholds the six broad quarters; the bull has entered into this entire world.

sanskrit: anaḍvān duhe sukṛtasya loka ainaṃ pyāyeta pavamānaḥ purastāt | parjanyo dhārā maruta ūdho asya yajñaḥ payo dakṣiṇā doho asya ||
english: The bull is milked for the realm of good deeds; may Pavamāna swell him from the east. Parjanya is the stream, the Maruts are his udder; sacrifice is the milk, the sacrificial fee is the milking.

sanskrit: anaḍvān indraḥ sa paśubhyo vi caṣṭe trayāṃ chakropa mimīte adhvanaḥ | sa bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyad bhuvanaṃ duhānaḥ sarvā devānāṃ bibhrac carati vratāni ||
english: The bull — he is Indra — surveys the beasts; he measures out the threefold path. Yielding milk of what has been and what shall be, bearing all the ordinances of the gods, he moves about.

sanskrit: yasya neśe yajñapatir na yajño nāsya dāteśe na pratigrahītā | yo viśvabhṛd viśvakarmā gharmaṃ no brūta yatamaś catuṣpāt ||
english: Of him neither the lord of sacrifice holds power, nor does sacrifice itself; neither the giver nor the receiver rules over him. He who bears all, who fashions all — tell us of the gharma vessel: which of the four-footed ones is he?

sanskrit: indra eṣa manuṣyeṣv antar gharmas taptaś carati śośucānaḥ | suprajā asat sa udāre na sarṣad yo nāśnīyād anaḍuho vijānan ||
english: This one is Indra; among human beings the heated gharma moves, blazing bright. He who, knowing it, would not eat of the bull's flesh shall not be stirred in his generous bounty — he shall be rich in offspring.

sanskrit: yena devāḥ svar āruruhur hitvā śarīram amṛtasya dhāma | tena geṣma sukṛtasya lokaṃ gharmasya vratena yaśasā tapasyayā ||
english: By that by which the gods ascended to heaven, having left the body — the abode of immortality — by that may we attain the realm of good deeds: by the vow of the gharma, by glory, by fervent austerity.

sanskrit: dvādaśaitā rātrīr vratyā āhuḥ prajāpateḥ | tatrāpi brahmaṇo vrataṃ tatrāpy anaḍuho balam ||
english: These twelve nights they call the observance nights of Prajāpati. Therein also is the vow of brahman; therein also is the strength of the bull.

sanskrit: yās ta āhuḥ prajāpater vratyā rātrīr dvādaśa | tatrāpi brahma yo veda tad vā anaḍuho balam ||
english: Those twelve observance nights of Prajāpati that they speak of — he who knows the brahman therein knows verily the strength of the bull.

sanskrit: duhe vā anaḍvān sāyaṃ duhe prātar duhe divā | dohā ye asya saṃyanti tān vidmānupadasvataḥ ||
english: The bull is milked at evening, milked at dawn, milked by day. Those milkings of his that come together — we know them from his followers.

sanskrit: yo vedānaḍuho dohān saptān upadasvataḥ | prajāṃ ca lokaṃ cāpnoti tathā sapta rṣayo viduḥ ||
english: He who knows the seven milkings of the bull through his devotees — he attains offspring and the heavenly realm; so indeed the seven ṛṣis know.

sanskrit: madhyam etad anaḍuho yatraiṣa vaha āhitaḥ | etāvad asya prācīnaṃ yāvān pratyaṅ samāhitaḥ ||
english: This is the middle part of the bull where his yoke-bar is set. His forward part extends as far as his hinder part is gathered in.

sanskrit: padbhiḥ sedim avakrāmann irāṃ jaṅghābhir utkhidan | śrameṇānaḍvān kīlālaṃ kīnāśaś cābhi gacchataḥ ||
english: Treading the ploughshare down with his hooves, churning up the soil with his shanks — by toil the bull and the ploughman together approach the sweet drink of refreshment.

sanskrit: indra eṣa manuṣyeṣv anaḍvān ity ucyate | śaphāso asya mā riṣan sarvā yāś cāsya kuṣṭhikāḥ ||
english: This one is called the bull among human beings; he is Indra. May his hooves not be harmed, nor any of his leg joints.

sanskrit: indro balenāsi parameṣṭhī vratena yena gaus tena vaiśvadevaḥ | yo asmān dveṣṭi yaṃ vayaṃ dviṣmas tasya prāṇān saṃ bṛhat tasya prāṇān vi vṛha ||
english: By strength thou art Indra, by vow thou art Parameṣṭhin; by that whereby the cow exists, thou art Vaiśvadeva. Him who hates us, whom we hate — crush together his vital breaths, tear asunder his vital breaths.

sanskrit: gṛhān aimi manasā modamāna ūrjaṃ bibhrad vasumaniḥ sumedhāḥ | aghoreṇa cakṣuṣā mitriyeṇa gṛhāṇāṃ paśyan paya ut tarāmi ||
english: I approach the houses rejoicing in my mind, bearing vigor, intent on wealth, of keen intelligence. Beholding the milk of the houses with a benign, friendly eye, I rise up.

sanskrit: ime gṛhā mayobhuva ūrjasvantaḥ payasvantaḥ | pūrṇā vāmasya tiṣṭhantas te no jānantu jānataḥ ||
english: These houses are sources of joy, full of vigor, full of milk, standing laden with good things — may they recognize us as those who know them.

sanskrit: sūnṛtāvantaḥ subhagā irāvanto hasāmudāḥ | akṣudhyā atṛṣyāso gṛhā māsmad bibhītana ||
english: Rich in pleasant words, blessed, food-abounding, glad with laughter — O houses free from hunger and thirst, be not afraid of us.

sanskrit: yeṣām adhyeti pravasan yeṣu saumanaso bahuḥ | gṛhān upa hvayāmahe te no jānantv āyataḥ ||
english: The houses to which one returns when traveling abroad, in which there is great goodwill — those houses we invite; may they know us as we arrive.

sanskrit: upahūtā iva gāva upahūtā ajāvayaḥ | atho annasya kīlāla upahūto gṛheṣu naḥ ||
english: As cattle are called home, as goats and sheep are called home — so too may the sweet drink of food be called home into our houses.

sanskrit: upahūtā bhūridhanāḥ sakhāyaḥ svādusaṃmudaḥ | ariṣṭāḥ sarvapūruṣā gṛhā naḥ santu sarvadā ||
english: Called in are friends of great wealth and sweet delight; unharmed and with all their folk, may our houses be so always.

sanskrit: hantāyam astv apratighātyaḥ sāsahvām̐ indraḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭhiḥ | prajāpatir adadhād ojo asmai bṛhad dhavir haviṣā vardhanena ||
english: May this one be a slayer, irresistible in attack — Indra who has prevailed, standing firm in battles. Prajāpati has bestowed upon him great vigor, the great oblation, growing strong through the offered oblation.

sanskrit: prajāpate haviṣā vardhanena hantāram indram akṛṇor aghātyam | tasmai viśo devakṛtā namanta sa hi hantā sa hi havyo babhūva ||
english: O Prajāpati, with the growth-conferring oblation thou hast made Indra a slayer, impossible to strike down. Before him the clans created by the gods bow down; for he verily is the smiter, he verily has become the one worthy of oblation.

sanskrit: prajāpate abhi no neṣa vasya urvīṃ gavyūtim abhimātiṣāhaḥ | vardhayann indraṃ bṛhate raṇāya devaṃ devena haviṣā vardhanena ||
english: O Prajāpati, lead us toward better fortune, to a wide cattle-pasture, O overcomer of assailants — strengthening Indra for great battle, the god with the god-strengthening oblation.

sanskrit: yathā viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ saṃjayāsi yathā śatrūn sahamānaḥ sahāsai | yathāsaḥ samrāṭ susamrāḍ evā tvendro 'prativadhaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: As thou shalt conquer all battle arrays, as thou shalt prevail overwhelming enemies, as thou shalt be sovereign, a great sovereign — even so may Indra make thee irresistible in smiting.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vīro 'prati hantu śatrūn viśve devā apa sadas karātha | māsya prajāṃ rīriṣan mota vīrān imam indro 'prativadhaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: May this hero smite enemies without check; all you gods, clear away his adversaries. Do not injure his offspring nor his heroes — may Indra make him irresistible in smiting.

sanskrit: jahi śatrūn prati randhayasva- -agniṣ ṭe gopā adhipā vasiṣṭhaḥ | śarma te rājā varuṇo ni yacchād evā tvendro 'prativadhaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: Strike the enemies, make them subject to thee — Agni is thy guardian, the most excellent overlord. May King Varuṇa grant thee shelter — even so may Indra make thee irresistible in smiting.
